To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the thick-strained-SI/SiGe CMOs technology has a 90 to 110-nM strained Si layer that is thicker than the limit for which misfit dislocation occurs and that has a new STI structure that has an SES layer to cover up SiGe trench surfaces.
the new technology is compatible with Si CMOS, has the same or better device characteristics as the usual thin-strained Si/SiGe technology, and is expected to be applied in the future.
a thick strained Si/Si1-xGex (x = 0.1) MOSFET has been successfully fabricated with a selective-epi-Si STI.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of thick-strained-SI/SiGe CMOST with a SES-STI structure.
the fabrication of thick-strained-S/SiGe CMOST with SES-STI.
the development of a new bulk strained-Si/Si _{1-x} Ge _{x} CMOS technology that can be applied to high-performance microprocessor applications.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
thick strained Si and SES-STI can be applied to Si CMOS without any problem and can provide the same performance enhancement as thin strained Si/SiGes.
the new bulk strained-Si CMOS technology is a promising candidate for future CMOS.
the new thick-strained-SI/SiGe CMOSTI is a promising candidate for the next generation of Si-based CMOS technology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a new technology is available for strained-Si/Si-Ge CMOS, which can be applied to a wide range of applications.
a new bulk strained-Si/Si-Ge CMOS technology is feasible without any Ge-related problems.
the thick-strained Si can replace the thin-strained Si and the new SES-STI structure can replace the conventional STI.
